title: applySticks ramps flightRoll at 2 dt and flightPitch at 4 dt toward the sticks and snaps onto them
derivation: A Viper-like ship (max roll 2.8, max pitch 1.8) in TUMBLE with stick_roll 2.8 and stick_pitch -1.8 from rest, accuracy 2 (below COMBAT_AI_TRACKS_CLOSER 7.5, so no extra doubling). behaviour_tumble only calls applySticks, whose per-tick limits are rate1 = 2 dt = 1/60 for roll and rate2 = 4 dt = 1/30 for pitch (ShipEntity.m:7021-7022), so flightRoll(k) = min(2.8, k/60) and flightPitch(k) = -min(1.8, k/30); the last step lands on the stick exactly because |stick - flight| is then at most one rate step (7042-7056). Ticks 168 and 54/55 sit at the ramp end, where the float32 and float64 ramps can differ by one rounding; the tolerance is the measured float32-versus-float64 difference. Closed forms, not simulation, give every expected value; the reference replays them. TUMBLE skips the speed ramp and the move, so the ship stays at the origin.

title: applySticks moves flightRoll four times faster while the stick opposes the current rate
derivation: TUMBLE with stick_roll -2.8 while flightRoll starts at +1.9 (accuracy 2). While the stick is negative and flightRoll positive the rate is quadrupled: rate1 = 4 * 2 dt = 1/15 per tick (ShipEntity.m:7025-7026), so flightRoll(k) = 1.9 - k/15 for k <= 29 (the 29th step is taken from +1/30 and still quadrupled, ending at -1/30). From tick 30 both are negative, so the plain 2 dt = 1/60 rate applies: flightRoll(k) = -1/30 - (k-29)/60 until the snap onto -2.8 at tick 195. The start value 1.9 puts the zero crossing mid-step (28.5 steps), away from any threshold, so the float32 and float64 runs take the same branch every tick.

title: applySticks at accuracy 8 with the stick at 0: the settle rate is doubled
derivation: TUMBLE with both sticks 0 and a starting flightRoll and flightPitch of 0.97, accuracy 8. accuracy >= COMBAT_AI_TRACKS_CLOSER (7.5): with a stick at exactly 0 the rate doubles, rate1 = 2 * 2 dt = 1/30 and rate2 = 2 * 4 dt = 1/15 (ShipEntity.m:7032-7039), so a tick-1 step is 1/30 for roll and 1/15 for pitch. The expected values are max(0, 0.97 - k * rate): the last step snaps onto the stick when the remainder is at most one rate step (7042-7056). The twin fixture sticks-accuracy-2-stick-zero is identical except for accuracy, so the pair isolates the factor 2. The start 0.97 is 29.1 or 58.2 roll steps and 14.55 or 29.1 pitch steps from zero (accuracy 8 or 2), so no snap lands on a threshold.

title: a positive flightRoll tilts the ship's up vector toward its own -right (Oolite quaternion maths)
derivation: TUMBLE with stick_roll = flightRoll = 1.0 rad/s, so every update keeps the rate and applyAttitudeChanges turns the ship by flightRoll * dt = 1/120 rad. applyRoll:climb:andYaw: builds q1 = rotate_about_z(identity, -roll) and sets orientation = q1 * orientation (ShipEntity.m:5886-5895); quaternion_rotate_about_z(identity, a) is (cos a/2, 0, 0, sin a/2) (OOQuaternion.m:327-343). Repeated k times the total rotation is a = -k/120 about z, so the quaternion is (cos(k/240), 0, 0, -sin(k/240)); vector_up_from_quaternion (OOQuaternion.m:89-120) gives up = (2wz, 1 - 2z^2, 0) = (-sin(k/120), cos(k/120), 0), and forward stays (0, 0, 1). So a positive flightRoll leans up toward -right (negative x): it rolls the ship's top to its left, the sense trackDestination uses when it chooses a NEGATIVE stick_roll for a target on the right (ShipEntity.m:9529-9531). Closed form, tolerance from the float32 versus float64 measurement.

title: a positive flightPitch tips the ship's nose toward its own -up (Oolite quaternion maths)
derivation: TUMBLE with stick_pitch = flightPitch = 0.5 rad/s: every update turns the ship by flightPitch * dt = 0.5/120 rad. applyRoll:climb:andYaw: uses rotate_about_x(q1, -climb) (ShipEntity.m:5890-5891); quaternion_rotate_about_x(identity, -t) is (cos t/2, -sin t/2, 0, 0) (OOQuaternion.m:291-307). After k updates t = 0.5 k/120, and vector_forward_from_quaternion (OOQuaternion.m:50-81) gives forward = (0, 2wx, 1 - 2x^2) = (0, -sin t, cos t); vector_up_from_quaternion gives up = (0, cos t, sin t). So a positive flightPitch tips the nose toward -up (down in Oolite's frame where up is +y), which is why trackDestination chooses a NEGATIVE stick_pitch for a target above (ShipEntity.m:9554). Closed form, tolerance from the float32 versus float64 measurement.

title: one update composes the roll and the climb as q1 = Rz(-roll) * Rx(-climb), then orientation = q1 * orientation
derivation: TUMBLE with stick_roll = flightRoll = 1.0 and stick_pitch = flightPitch = 0.5, so each update applies phi = 1/120 and theta = 0.5/120. ShipEntity.m:5886-5895 starts q1 at the identity, rotates about z by -phi, then about x by -theta, and multiplies q1 on the left of the orientation. rotate_about_axis(q, a) is q * R(a) (OOQuaternion.m:331-342), so q1 = Rz(-phi) * Rx(-theta) = (cr cp, -cr sp, sr sp, -sr cp) with cr = cos(phi/2), sr = sin(phi/2), cp = cos(theta/2), sp = sin(theta/2). Tick 1 is q1 itself, tick 2 is q1 * q1 (the two rotations do not commute, so tick 2 is not a doubling of the angles). Forward and up come from the OOQuaternion.m:50-120 formulas written out on the double-precision product. Closed form; tolerance from the float32 versus float64 measurement.

title: applyThrust ramps flightSpeed at 5 * thrust per second to desiredSpeed and holds it
derivation: An IDLE ship at rest with desired_speed 320 (the Viper-like max_flight_speed) and thrust 32. dt_thrust = SHIP_THRUST_FACTOR * thrust * dt = 5 * 32 / 120 = 4/3 per tick (ShipEntity.m:5810), increase_flight_speed adds it (7411-7414) and applyThrust clamps to desired_speed (5838-5842), so flightSpeed(k) = min(320, 4k/3): the ramp takes 240 ticks (2 s = maxFlightSpeed / (5 thrust)). moveForward(dt * flightSpeed) runs after the ramp update (5843), along the identity nose +z, so positionZ(k) = sum over j <= k of speed_j / 120 = k(k+1)/180 for k <= 240, then 320/120 per further tick. Tick 240 is the end of the ramp, where float32 and float64 may differ by one rounding step; the tolerance is the measured difference.

title: applyThrust clamps flightSpeed onto desiredSpeed in the same tick it would pass it
derivation: IDLE from rest with desired_speed 190 (below max_flight_speed 320) and thrust 32: the ramp adds 4/3 per tick, so tick 142 holds 189.3333 and the tick-143 update would reach 190.667, which applyThrust clamps back to 190 (ShipEntity.m:5840-5841); every later tick holds 190. 190 / (4/3) = 142.5 steps, so the clamp happens mid-step, away from any float threshold. title: decrease_flight_speed uses MIN_HYPERSPEED_FACTOR (32) only while flightSpeed is above maxFlightSpeed
derivation: IDLE with flightSpeed 350 above max_flight_speed 320 and desired_speed 100. decrease_flight_speed uses factor MIN_HYPERSPEED_FACTOR = 32 (PlayerEntity.h:296) while flightSpeed > maxFlightSpeed (ShipEntity.m:7420-7422): tick 1 subtracts 32 * 4/3 = 42.667, leaving 307.333, which is below 320, so every later step uses factor 1 (4/3): flightSpeed(k) = 307.333 - (k-1) * 4/3 down to the clamp onto 100 at tick 157 (tick 156 holds 100.667; 207.333 / (4/3) = 155.5 steps, mid-step).
